shortSummary: Fragrant night-opening white vine-shrub of the olive family celebrated for jasmine tea scenting, attar perfumery, and ceremonial garlands.
leadOverview: Arabian Jasmine (Jasminum sambac)—beloved across Bengal and South Asia as Beli or Bela—is a compact scrambling shrub in the olive family (Oleaceae). Opening waxy star-like white blossoms at dusk that release an intoxicating indole-linalool perfume, it anchors Asia's luxury floral perfumery and traditional jasmine tea harvests.

sections.title: Morphological Description
sections.subtitle: Opposite glossy leaves, tubular white corollas, and double-whorled cultivars
sections.summary: Botanical structure of climbing stems, whorled leaves, night-fragrant blooms, and double mutants.
paragraphs: Jasminum sambac grows as an evergreen semi-climbing shrub with slender, softly pubescent green stems reaching 1 to 3 metres when supported. Its thin, glossy ovate leaves measure 4 to 10 centimetres long and are borne either in opposite pairs or in characteristic whorls of three along the nodes, with prominent arcuate lateral veins.

Flowers emerge in terminal cymes of 3 to 12 buds. Each blossom consists of a narrow tubular base flaring into 5 to 9 pure white oval lobes (or dense rose-like concentric petal whorls in double cultivars such as 'Grand Duke of Tuscany') that gradually blush pale lilac-pink as they age.

subblocks.heading: Scrambling Stems
subblocks.text: Slender woody-based green shoots displaying mild pubescence and arching climbing habit.

subblocks.heading: Leaves & Nodes
subblocks.text: Ovate-elliptic glossy blades arranged oppositely or in ternate whorls of three with short curved petioles.

subblocks.heading: Nocturnal Corolla
subblocks.text: Waxy white salverform flowers opening at twilight with two concealed stamens inside the floral tube.

subblocks.heading: Berries & Roots
subblocks.text: Rarely set twin globose black berries (many double forms are sterile); vigorous fibrous root system.

sections.title: Taxonomy & Botanical Classification
sections.subtitle: Lamiales order and Oleaceae cultivar taxonomy
sections.summary: Taxonomic kinship with olives and lilacs plus key ornamental cultivars.
paragraphs: Classified within order Lamiales and the olive family (Oleaceae), Jasminum sambac is related to Olea europaea (olive), Syringa (lilac), and Nyctanthes arbor-tristis (night-flowering coral jasmine). Unlike many plants mistakenly labelled jasmine (such as toxic yellow Gelsemium or Madagascar stephanotis), true Jasminum species possess two-stamen tubular flowers and non-toxic foliage.
Horticulturally, three main clones dominate: single-petalled 'Maid of Orleans' (prized for tea scenting), semi-double 'Belle of India', and heavily doubled 'Grand Duke of Tuscany'.

sections.title: Natural Habitat & Global Distribution
sections.subtitle: South Asian monsoon plains to Fujian tea-scenting valleys
sections.summary: Origin in tropical South Asia and historic spread to China, Southeast Asia, and Middle East.
paragraphs: Originating in tropical regions of the Indian subcontinent and Myanmar, Jasminum sambac thrives in warm, humid monsoon lowlands with rich alluvial soil and distinct summer warmth. Centuries ago, maritime and overland spice routes carried living cuttings eastward to China and Southeast Asia, and westward across Arabia.
In Bangladesh, commercial Beli flower farms flourish around Jashore's Godkhali floral belt and Savar, supplying fresh evening buds to urban flower markets every dawn.

sections.title: Ecological Role & Pollinator Interactions
sections.subtitle: Twilight scent synthesis and nocturnal hawkmoth pollination
sections.summary: Circadian aroma emission synchronized with crepuscular moth activity.
paragraphs: Jasminum sambac regulates its perfume biosynthesis via a strict circadian clock: unopened buds harvested in late afternoon remain nearly scentless until twilight temperatures cool, triggering enzymatic release of benzyl acetate, indole, cis-jasmone, and linalool.
Pure white petals gleam in moonlight while narrow floral tubes guide nocturnal sphinx moths and crepuscular bees straight to deep basal nectar rewards.

sections.title: Economic, Culinary & Cultural Importance
sections.subtitle: Jasmine tea scenting, Bengali wedding gajra garlands, and solvent extraction
sections.summary: Multi-million-dollar floral fragrance crop and beloved cultural heirloom across Asia.
paragraphs: In Chinese and Vietnamese tea craft, freshly plucked evening Beli buds are layered repeatedly over dried Camellia sinensis green tea leaves overnight so warm tea leaves absorb the rising nocturnal perfume—producing classic Jasmine Pearls and scented oolongs. Concurrently, concrete and absolute oils extracted from blooms anchor prestige global perfumery.

Culturally, Jasminum sambac is the national flower of the Philippines (Sampaguita) and Indonesia (Melati Putih), and across Bangladesh and India, braided white Beli gajra garlands adorn brides, classical dancers, and festive gatherings.

sections.title: Traditional & Scientific Medicinal Properties
sections.subtitle: Linalool aromatherapy, calming infusions, and cutaneous cooling
sections.summary: Aromatherapeutic relaxation and mild antimicrobial compounds in flowers and leaves.
paragraphs: Traditional Unani and Ayurvedic medicine utilize jasmine flower compresses and gentle floral waters (Ruh-e-Motia) to cool irritated eyes, soothe nervous tension, and calm minor skin inflammation. Essential-oil constituents include linalool, benzyl benzoate, farnesene, and phytol.

Psychophysiological aromatherapy trials indicate that inhaling jasmine volatiles can modestly elevate parasympathetic calm and alertness balance, while leaf extracts demonstrate mild antimicrobial properties in vitro.
sections.safetyNote: True Jasminum sambac flowers are food-safe for tea scenting, whereas ornamental lookalikes such as Carolina Jessamine (Gelsemium sempervirens) are highly poisonous. Always verify botanical identity and keep concentrated jasmine absolute oils properly diluted before skin contact.

sections.title: Comprehensive Cultivation & Care Guide
sections.subtitle: Full sun, deadheading, post-bloom pruning, and spider-mite hygiene
sections.summary: Growing profusely blooming Beli shrubs in gardens and sunny balconies.
paragraphs: Provide Jasminum sambac with 5 to 6 hours of direct morning-to-midday sun and fertile, humus-rich, well-drained soil (pH 6.0–7.0). Water consistently during active summer budding without letting pots sit waterlogged, and feed every 3 to 4 weeks with balanced organic compost or potassium-rich bloom feed.

Because flowers form exclusively on new terminal shoots, snip spent flower trusses cleanly just above a healthy leaf node and perform a structural prune after the main monsoon flush to keep shrubs compact and profusely budded.

sections.title: Annual Phenology & Six-Season Rhythms
sections.subtitle: Flowering, fruiting, vegetative flush, and Shororitu synchrony
sections.summary: Seasonal cadence across Bengal's six-season cycle (Spring (বসন্ত), Summer (গ্রীষ্ম), Monsoon (বর্ষা)).
paragraphs: Jasmine (Beli) (Jasminum sambac) aligns its vegetative flushes, anthesis, and fruit maturation tightly with Bengal's Shororitu photoperiod and monsoon moisture transitions, showing peak biological activity during Spring (বসন্ত), Summer (গ্রীষ্ম), Monsoon (বর্ষা).

Spring (বসন্ত): Spring warmth awakens pruned woody canes into prolific white bud initiation. Summer (গ্রীষ্ম): Peak dusk opening releases intoxicating benzyl acetate perfume prized for summer evening garlands. Monsoon (বর্ষা): Monsoon moisture extends successive flushes of star-white corollas amidst deep green leaves.

subblocks.text: Synchronized with daylength shifts, pre-monsoon thermal buildup, and seasonal soil moisture oscillations.

sections.title: Seed Germination Biology & Propagation
sections.subtitle: Dormancy regulation, nursery media, and clonal propagation
sections.summary: Reproductive biology and reliable seed or vegetative propagation techniques for Jasmine (Beli).
paragraphs: Jasmine (Beli) (Jasminum sambac) exhibits dual reproductive versatility through wind-, pollinator-, or gravity-dispersed seed cohorts alongside rapid vegetative renewal via herbaceous stem cuttings, rhizome splits, or nodal rooting. Mature seed capsules collected just prior to dehiscence retain strong vigor in dry shaded storage for moderate periods.
Rooting auxin pre-treatment on semi-ripe nodal cuttings during warm humid months accelerates adventitious root initiation within 10 to 21 days in porous coco-peat and vermicompost propagation trays.

subblocks.heading: Seed Germination
subblocks.text: Surface-sown or lightly covered in sterile porous mix; germinates in 7–21 days under ambient humidity.

subblocks.heading: Vegetative Method
subblocks.text: Two-node terminal cuttings or clump division rooted in misted, filtered-light benches.

sections.title: Pathology Defense, Vectors & Organic IPM
sections.subtitle: Phytoalexin resilience, fungal prophylaxis, and predator guilds
sections.summary: Biochemical defense mechanisms and low-impact organic IPM guidelines for Jasminum sambac.
paragraphs: In humid South Asian and tropical growing belts, Jasmine (Beli) (Jasminum sambac) relies on secondary terpenoid resins, foliar trichomes, and phytoalexin phenolics as front-line biochemical deterrence against herbivores and opportunistic pathogens. Prolonged monsoon waterlogging or stagnant canopy humidity can nonetheless encourage anthracnose (Colletotrichum spp.), powdery mildew, leaf-spot fungi, or root-zone Pythium.

Organic Integrated Pest Management (IPM) prioritizes preventive airflow pruning, Trichoderma-enriched compost amendments around feeder roots, and targeted cold-pressed Azadirachta indica (neem) oil sprays at dusk to suppress sap-sucking aphids, scale insects, and mealybugs without harming native pollinators.

subblocks.heading: Fungal Management
subblocks.text: Prevent overhead foliar wetness at dusk; maintain canopy aeration and copper/Trichoderma prophylaxis.

subblocks.heading: Organic Pest Control
subblocks.text: Neem kernel emulsion (3–5 ml/L) plus conservation of hoverfly and ladybird predator guilds.

sections.title: Conservation Standing & Climate Resilience
sections.subtitle: Population security, agroforestry corridors, and stress tolerance
sections.summary: Biogeographic conservation standing and climate adaptation traits of Jasmine (Beli).
paragraphs: Across its native and naturalized distribution (South & Southeast Asia), Jasmine (Beli) (Jasminum sambac) demonstrates strong ecological plasticity across alluvial floodplains, homestead agroforestry plots, and urban biodiversity corridors. While cultivated stands remain broadly secure, landrace genetic erosion, coastal salinity shifts, and wetland drainage threaten wild ecotypes and heritage regional varieties.

Long-term resilience depends on decentralized in-situ homestead stewardship, wetland buffer conservation, and botanical garden germplasm collections preserving drought-, flood-, and salinity-tolerant alleles amid shifting monsoon regimes.

subblocks.heading: Ecological Resilience
subblocks.text: Adapted to South & Southeast Asia thermal oscillations and seasonal hydrological extremes.

subblocks.heading: Stewardship Strategy
subblocks.text: Preserve traditional landraces, pollinator corridors, and living herbarium voucher plots.

sections.title: Horticultural Spacing, Pruning & Telemetry
sections.subtitle: Plot geometry, canopy shaping, and calibrated soil-climate meters
sections.summary: Calibrated horticultural parameters: pH 6.0 – 7.2 (Slightly acidic to neutral), Full Sun to Partial Filtered Light (6+ hrs), and structural spacing guidance.
paragraphs: Optimal managed cultivation of Jasmine (Beli) (Jasminum sambac) calibrates root-zone chemistry around pH 6.0 – 7.2 (Slightly acidic to neutral) inside well-drained organic sandy-clay loam. Providing adequate crown spacing prevents humidity buildup and lets lower shoots capture uniform irradiance across full sun to partial filtered light (6+ hrs).

Light corrective pruning immediately after main flowering or harvest periods redirects assimilates into healthy vegetative framework, while moisture scheduling (moderate deep watering scaled to monsoon rhythm) stabilizes root turgor without inducing hypoxia.

sections.title: Evolutionary Genetics & Adaptive Phylogeny
sections.subtitle: Lamiales clade divergence and Oleaceae genomic traits
sections.summary: Phylogenetic placement of genus Jasminum within order Lamiales (Eudicot (Lamiids)).
paragraphs: Modern molecular phylogenetics (APG IV) places Jasminum sambac inside family Oleaceae (ওলিয়াসি (বেলি-জলপাই গোত্র)), order Lamiales, clade Eudicot (Lamiids). Olive and jasmine woody climbers and trees recognized by opposite leaves and intensely fragrant, star-like white corollas rich in benzyl acetate.

Within genus Jasminum, specialized morphological adaptations—such as opposite simple or trifoliate leaves without stipules—reflect co-evolutionary specialization with regional pollinator guilds and abiotic habitat filters.

sections.title: Field Identification Key & Diagnostic Checks
sections.subtitle: Macro-morphological verification against look-alike taxa
sections.summary: Rapid field-sheet checklist for confirming Jasminum sambac (Beli (বেলি)).
paragraphs: Field verification of Jasmine (Beli) (Jasminum sambac) rests on recognizing key Oleaceae family markers: Opposite simple or trifoliate leaves without stipules; Nocturnal fragrance release timed for crepuscular moth pollination; Paired stamens attached inside slender tubular floral throats. Inspecting fresh leaf arrangement, stem surface texture, and reproductive architecture together eliminates confusion with sympatric congeners.
